study: Cordray et al. 2012 (NWEA MAP benchmark assessment + teacher training/coaching; reading)
eval_evidence: Independent NCEE/IES evaluation by REL Midwest (Learning Point Associates, an AIR affiliate); report NCEE 2013-4000. NWEA (developer) only provided implementation support and commented on a draft.
developer_evidence: NWEA (the MAP developer) delivered the teacher training and provided the on-site MAP coach: 'NWEA provides training sessions and face-to-face consultative services. MAP training consists of four one-day sessions, along with on-demand consultation... and on-site visits from an NWEA MAP coach.'
cascade_evidence: NWEA trainers/coach trained the teachers directly (four one-day NWEA sessions + NWEA MAP coach), no intermediary cascade.
counterfactual_evidence: Control = business-as-usual schools with no benchmark/MAP-style assessment or training (design note). Appendix L assessed and addressed control-group contamination; grade-4 confirmatory contrast treated as clean BAU.
coaching_evidence: Support was an NWEA MAP coach providing on-demand consultation and on-site visits, with the option of three to four consultative sessions across the school year (data-interpretation/differentiation consultation), not recurring in-class instructional coaching cycles.
student_dose_evidence: The student-facing element is periodic NWEA computer-adaptive benchmark assessment (a few times/year), not added instruction; the intervention is teacher data-use training/coaching, so the teacher's regular reading instruction is what changes.
maturity_evidence: Two-year implementation; impacts measured at end of Year 2 (spring 2010), after a prior Year-1 implementation year (Year-1 was interim).
